title: Build a Public VPC Foundation
scenario: Assemble a minimal public VPC: VPC, public subnet, internet gateway, route table with a default route, and an association.
constraints: One VPC, one public subnet, one IGW, one route table and one association.

focus.title: Complete the aws_subnet resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_subnet.

hints.why: A VPC is the network boundary for most AWS resources. CIDR planning, subnets and routing decisions affect everything deployed inside it.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_subnet" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_subnet. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Design a VPC when you need isolated networking, predictable address space or control over public and private traffic.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_subnet" "this"`. Use this code shape: cidr_block; tags; vpc_id; availability_zone; map_public_ip_on_launch. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.project_name`, `var.environment`, `aws_vpc.this.id`, `var.availability_zone`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
